experiments.description: Warm-start QAOA on synthetic portfolio-optimization instances using a continuous quadratic relaxation to initialize the quantum state and a modified warm-start mixer.

algorithm.variant: Warm-start QAOA (WS-QAOA) with continuous relaxation initialization
algorithm.ansatz: Layered QAOA with problem unitary exp(-i gamma_k H_C) and warm-start mixer exp(-i beta_k H_M^(ws))

hyperparameters.epsilon: varied; main comparisons include epsilon in [0, 0.5], with epsilon = 0.25 highlighted
hyperparameters.beta_gamma_search: COBYLA seeded with random initial guesses

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state prepared from the continuous relaxation solution c* via single-qubit RY rotations; beta and gamma initialized randomly uniform from ±2π for COBYLA.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per binary decision variable x_i with x_i = (1 - z_i)/2; mapped to an Ising Hamiltonian.
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize q x^T Sigma x - mu^T x subject to 1^T x = B, implemented with a quadratic penalty lambda (1^T x - B)^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Budget constraint enforced by large quadratic penalty term lambda(1^T x - B)^2
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising Hamiltonian H_C derived from q x^T Sigma x - mu^T x + lambda(1^T x - B)^2

problem_instance.description: Random synthetic portfolio instances generated from simulated asset prices and solved at multiple QAOA depths; one representative instance has d* = (0,0,1,1,1,0) and c* ≃ (0.17, 0, 0.97, 0.73, 1.0, 0.14).

dataset_specification.description: Asset prices simulated with Geometric Brownian motion for N = 250 days; means mu_i sampled uniformly from [-5%, 5%], standard deviations sigma_i sampled uniformly from [-20%, 20%], initial prices set to 1; returns and covariance computed from simulated time series.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute daily returns from simulated prices, then mean returns and covariance matrix; enforce budget constraint with penalty lambda = 3.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single representative instance across depths p = 1..5; optimized energy and probability of sampling the optimal bitstring reported; QAOA run ten times with different random initial guesses.

noise_model.noise_description: ideal statevector simulation; no noise model reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Solve continuous relaxation with CPLEX to obtain c*; simulate portfolio prices with Geometric Brownian motion; compute covariance matrix and returns; map to Ising Hamiltonian.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Diagonalize H_C to obtain minimum energy E0; compare optimized energies E*_cold and E*_warm; compute probability of sampling the optimal binary solution.

speedup_claims.caveats: No computational speedup claim; the paper reports improved solution quality and higher probability of sampling the optimal portfolio at low depth.

scalability_data.metric_value: more than 5x higher than standard QAOA

experiments.description: Warm-start QAOA on synthetic portfolio instances using the same continuous relaxation but replacing the warm-start mixer with the standard X mixer to test the role of the modified mixer.

algorithm.ansatz: QAOA with initial state from continuous relaxation and standard mixer -sum X_i

hyperparameters.epsilon: continuous solution c* used for initialization; epsilon not central in this variant

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state prepared from continuous relaxation solution c*; beta and gamma initialized randomly uniform from ±2π.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per binary decision variable x_i with x_i = (1 - z_i)/2.
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize q x^T Sigma x - mu^T x subject to 1^T x = B, with penalty lambda(1^T x - B)^2
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising Hamiltonian H_C derived from the portfolio QUBO

problem_instance.description: Same synthetic 6-asset portfolio instances as the main warm-start experiment, used to isolate the effect of the mixer choice.

dataset_specification.description: Geometric Brownian motion simulation over N = 250 days; mu_i in [-5%, 5%], sigma_i in [-20%, 20%].

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare optimized energy and optimal-solution probability against WS-QAOA with warm-start mixer and standard QAOA.

noise_model.noise_description: ideal statevector simulation; no noise model reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Continuous relaxation solved with CPLEX; same synthetic data generation as exp_1.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Diagonalization for E0; compare energy and sampling probability.

speedup_claims.caveats: This experiment isolates the effect of replacing the warm-start mixer with the standard X mixer; no speedup claim is made.

scalability_data.metric_value: does not converge to minimum energy with standard mixer

experiments.description: Depth-one warm-start QAOA on 250 random synthetic portfolio instances to compare warm-start versus standard QAOA statistically.

algorithm.variant: Depth-one WS-QAOA versus standard QAOA on many random portfolio instances

hyperparameters.epsilon: warm-start setting; not explicitly varied in this experiment

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Warm-start from continuous relaxation solution c*; standard QAOA initialized from equal superposition.

problem_formulation.objective_function: min q x^T Sigma x - mu^T x with budget constraint 1^T x = B enforced by penalty

problem_instance.description: 250 random portfolio instances generated synthetically; q = 2 in the reported histogram experiment.

dataset_specification.description: Randomly generated asset price paths via Geometric Brownian motion; each instance has 6 assets.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute covariance and returns from simulated prices; solve continuous relaxation with CPLEX.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 250 instances; each QAOA run ten times with different random initial guesses; report histograms of normalized energy and dependence on overlap d*^T c*/B.

noise_model.noise_description: ideal statevector simulation; no noise model reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Synthetic data generation and continuous relaxation solved with CPLEX.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Direct diagonalization for E0; compute energy ratios and optimal-solution probabilities.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports improved solution quality and higher optimal-solution probability for WS-QAOA at depth 1, but no runtime speedup.

scalability_data.metric_value: WS-QAOA histogram concentrated closer to E0 than standard QAOA

experiments.description: Warm-start QAOA for MAXCUT using Goemans-Williamson rounded cuts as the initial state, evaluated on fully connected random weighted graphs.

algorithm.variant: Warm-start QAOA for MAXCUT with Goemans-Williamson rounding
algorithm.ansatz: Depth-one QAOA with modified warm-start mixer that can recover the GW cut

hyperparameters.mixer: modified warm-start mixer with sign-flipped off-diagonal terms

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Grid search over gamma1 with 25 points and beta1 in {3pi/4, 3pi/8}; best point used to seed COBYLA.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per graph node; binary variable z_i in {-1,1} indicates cut side.
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize (1/2) sum_{(i,j) in E} omega_ij (1 - z_i z_j)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints beyond binary cut variables

problem_instance.description: Ten fully connected random weighted graphs with 30 nodes each; edge weights uniformly chosen from integers -10 to 10.

dataset_specification.description: Fully connected graphs; weights sampled uniformly from {-10, ..., 10}.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Generate 10 GW cuts per graph and keep the 5 best unique cuts for warm-starting.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: For each graph and each epsilon, optimize depth-one WS-QAOA and report normalized energy relative to the maximum cut.

noise_model.noise_description: ideal simulation; no noise model reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: GW randomized rounding used to generate candidate cuts; grid search used to seed COBYLA.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Normalize energies to the maximum cut found by CPLEX.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper suggests WS-QAOA may outperform GW rounding at some epsilon values, but this is a solution-quality comparison, not a speedup claim.

experiments.description: Warm-start Recursive QAOA (WS-RQAOA) for MAXCUT on random sparse and fully connected graphs, using GW-rounded cuts to initialize the recursive elimination procedure.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Warm-start from the best M unique GW cuts; each initializes a WS-QAOA run.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: MAXCUT on graph G=(V,E) with one logical qubit per node.
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize (1/2) sum_{(i,j) in E} omega_ij (1 - z_i z_j)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Recursive elimination replaces one variable z_i with sign(M_ij) z_j at each step
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising MAXCUT Hamiltonian H = (1/4) sum_{i,j} omega_ij (1 - Z_i Z_j)

problem_instance.description: Two families of synthetic graphs: 100 random graphs with 20 nodes and 100 with 30 nodes for each family; one family has edge probability pE = 1/2 and unit weights ±1, the other is fully connected with weights uniformly sampled from {-10, ..., 10}.

dataset_specification.description: Random graph ensembles as described above.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: At each recursion step, GW pre-solver generates 10 cuts; retain 5 best unique cuts; compute correlation matrix from WS-QAOA samples; reduce graph until nstop = n/2, then solve reduced problem by diagonalization.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare WS-RQAOA against standard RQAOA and a classical recursive GW-based baseline over 100 random graphs per setting.

noise_model.noise_description: ideal simulation; no noise model reported

implementation_details.classical_solver: CPLEX (for final reduced subproblem and reference maximum cuts)
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: GW pre-solver generates candidate cuts; correlation matrix computed from WS-QAOA samples; recursive variable elimination performed.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Diagonalize reduced Hamiltonian at nstop = n/2 and back-substitute recursive replacements.

speedup_claims.caveats: No runtime speedup is claimed; the result is improved cut quality and more maximum cuts found by WS-RQAOA relative to standard RQAOA.

scalability_data.metric_value: distribution of cut sizes over 100 graphs
